question: If \(i^2=-1,\) then \[ \left(i-i^{-1}\right)^{-1}= \]
solution:
An exponent of \(-1\) means reciprocal. Since \(i^2=-1\), we have \(i\ne0\), and
\[
i(-i)=-i^2=1.
\]
Thus \(i^{-1}=-i\), making the inner difference \(i-(-i)=2i\), which is also nonzero. To take its reciprocal, multiply numerator and denominator by \(-i\):
\[
\left(i-i^{-1}\right)^{-1}
=\frac{1}{2i}
=\frac{-i}{-2i^2}
=-\frac{i}{2}.
\]
The answer is \(\boxed{-\frac{i}{2}}\), choice \(\boxed{\text{D}}\).
